rationale: Ground truth is really two threads from Gaohan123: (P1) the live 501 mapping needs verification since omni_wakeup doesn't locally convert NotImplementedError, and (P2) the CPU mock test only proves route propagation, not the real level-2 engine contract. Y independently re-derives P1's resolution mechanism (finds vLLM's app.exception_handler(NotImplementedError) and traces create_error_response's 501 mapping) and explicitly restates P2's core critique, then extends it with a concrete, well-evidenced consequence (the real engine-level regression test moved from a per-PR merge gate to weekly-only CI). X's structured audit validates the 501 mapping is correct but frames it as settled fact rather than a flagged concern, and never surfaces the P2 issue at all — its 'validated' bullet for the mock test presents it approvingly with no critique of scope. Both candidates independently find solid, diff-grounded technical issues absent from the ground truth (vacuous VRAM asserts measuring the wrong process, _ensure_awake swallowing failures, missing inter-class GPU-clear wait, dropped TP=2/default-config diffusion coverage) with comparable precision and specific file:line evidence, but Y adds further well-verified findings (an actual pytest --collect-only run showing core_model/advanced_model double-selection, a num_cards=1 vs 2-device fixture mismatch, and an inverted code comment) and gives more concrete, copy-pasteable remediation. Y's clearer match to the ground-truth concerns plus its broader, similarly rigorous coverage make it the stronger review.
